q1_issues.issue: `Most` is specified as `(Most <scale> X <class>)` "plus X is a member of the class", but X here is a group witness and no class-membership companion is (or could be) emitted — a group of sentences is not itself a sentence, so the atom reads as "this group is the single simplest sentence".

The equative predication "the simplest ones ARE the most elegant ones" is carried only by re-using one symbol; no copular atom records the identity, and the second `Most` inherits the same group-in-entity-slot problem as the first.

q2_gaps: identity / equative copular clause ("The Xs are the Ys", two definite descriptions equated) — Categorical statements covers only "X is a/an N" and "X is ADJ"
superlative over a plural set ("the simplest sentences") — `Most` is defined for one entity X ranked in a class, with no form for the set of top-ranked members
one-anaphora on a plural ("the most elegant ones") used as a predicate nominal rather than introducing a fresh entity
notes: The definite-plural determiner rule forces a specific-group reading of what is really a generic aphorism; that is what the instruction set as written mandates, so it is not scored as a defect, but the 1.0/0.99 TVs then also follow the individual-fact branch rather than the empirical-generic dial.
